title: What is the total of notes of 100, 20 and 5 rupees?
description: {{NAME_9}} counts notes of one hundred, twenty and five rupees. The video completes the rows of a table by multiplying each number of notes by its value and adding, and then checks one row with a number in place of a letter.
teaching_notes: One idea: the total of money is the sum of each number of notes times the value of one note, even when the number is a letter. Watch for students who add the numbers of notes without the values.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of the bill expression: each kind of note is a number times its value, and the totals are added, with letters in place of unknown numbers.
video_script.substitution: The method of the bill expression, with three kinds of notes in place of two kinds of goods.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_9}}'s table of notes of one hundred, twenty and five rupees
video_script.payoff_line: Row one comes to four hundred and thirty rupees

final_answer.spoken: row one is four hundred and thirty, row two is six hundred and ninety five, row three is eight hundred and eighty plus five z, and row four is one hundred x plus twenty y plus five z

never_show: the totals of rows one, three and four before the answer beat
video_script.design: One idea: total money is the sum of number times value for each kind of note. Assumes the bill method with two kinds of goods. The table stays on the stage and the rows are filled in one by one. No wrong idea is raised.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a table with three columns for notes of 100, 20 and 5 rupees, and four rows, some cells holding letters

marks.p1: the title card From your book arrives
marks.p2: the table with its three columns and four rows appears
marks.p3: the cells with letters are highlighted
marks.p4: a question mark appears beside the empty total column

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>{{NAME_9}} has notes of one hundred, twenty and five rupees. A table shows how many notes of each kind.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>In some rows, the numbers of notes are letters.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>How can we find the total amount in every row?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: three stacks of notes with their values 100, 20 and 5 written on them; the second row of the table is already filled in

marks.g1: the three stacks of notes appear with their values
marks.g2: the money in one stack is shown as the number of notes times one note
marks.g3: the second row of the table, already worked, is highlighted

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>The money in one kind of note is the number of notes times its value.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>A row total is the sum of the money in the three kinds.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The second row is already worked in the book. It comes to six hundred and ninety five rupees.

beats.on_screen: Given: row 1: 3, 5, 6 notes ; row 3: 8, 4, z notes ; row 4: x, y, z notes

marks.gv1: the numbers of notes of row one are written
marks.gv2: the numbers of notes of rows three and four are written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, row one has three, five and six notes of the three kinds.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>Row three has eight, four and z notes. Row four has x, y and z notes.

beats.on_screen: To find: the total amount in rows 1, 3 and 4
narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We find the total in rows one, three and four. We use the method of the bill.

marks.s1a: 3 × 100 is written for the first kind of note
marks.s1b: 5 × 20 and 6 × 5 are written for the other two kinds

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Three notes of one hundred rupees are three times one hundred.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Five notes of twenty rupees are five times twenty. Six notes of five rupees are six times five.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Together, that is three hundred plus one hundred plus thirty.

marks.s2b: z × 5 is written for the last kind of note
marks.s2c: the three amounts 800 + 80 + z × 5 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Eight notes of one hundred rupees are eight hundred. Four notes of twenty rupees are eighty.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>The z notes of five rupees are z times five.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Together, that is eight hundred plus eighty plus z times five.

marks.s3b: y × 20 and z × 5 are written to complete the row

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>In row four, x notes of one hundred rupees are x times one hundred.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>The y notes of twenty rupees are y times twenty. The z notes of five rupees are z times five.

marks.s4a: z is replaced by 2 in row three

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Check row three with z as two notes of five rupees.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>The row gives eight hundred plus eighty plus ten. That is eight hundred and ninety.

marks.ans: the total of row one is boxed in the table
marks.ans2: the total of row two is boxed
marks.ans3: the total of row three is boxed
marks.ans4: the total of row four is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Row one comes to four hundred and thirty rupees.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Row two is six hundred and ninety five rupees.
<bookmark mark='ans3'/>Row three is eight hundred and eighty plus five z. That agrees with the check.
<bookmark mark='ans4'/>Row four is one hundred x plus twenty y plus five z.
